newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi 1997 budget raises spending, narrows deficit.
newsitem.headline: Saudi 1997 budget raises spending, narrows deficit.

text.p: Saudi Arabia on Monday issued a 1997 budget that raises expenditure to 181 billion riyals ($48 billion) and narrows the deficit to 17 billion riyals from 18.5 billion in 1996.
The kingdom predicted higher revenues at 164 billion riyals in 1997, up from 131.5 billion in 1996.
The 1996 budget had put expenditure at 150 billion riyals.
The budget was announced by King Fahd at a cabinet meeting on Monday night and was carried by the official Saudi Press Agency.
The decrees commissioned the Saudi Finance and Economy Ministry to borrow to meet the 1997 deficit.

King Fahd told the cabinet meeting that the 1997 budget was an important step towards achieving a balanced budget -- which Saudi Arabia has said it aims to do by the end of the century -- and asserting the strength of the economy.

Revenue and expenditure for the electricity sector was put at 688.5 million riyals, up from 610.5 million in 1996. The sector is involved in several multi-billion-dollar power-generating projects to meet growing demand.
Revenue and expenditure for the national flag carrier Saudi Arabian Airlines was put at 9 billion riyals, up from 8.48 billion riyals in 1996.
The budget decrees issued so far did not disclose how much was allocated for defence and security spending which traditionally account for about a third of the budget.
Economists and bankers in Saudi Arabia had predicted a narrower deficit in 1997 due to higher oil prices, the main source of income for the world's largest oil producer and exporter.
